capabilities: Review notes with AI editor personas that anchor findings to exact text spans
Apply AI-proposed changes through labelled diffs with accept, dismiss, and push-back replies
Group editors into panels that review together and produce a scorecard
Run action verbs on selections such as rephrase, summarize, humanize, and critique
Park margin comments that editors answer in the background
extras: Desktop only (Windows, macOS, Linux) and requires Obsidian 1.13.0 or newer. Bring-your-own backend: at least one hosted API key or a local agent CLI is needed. The manifest notes it has not been manually reviewed by Obsidian staff, and the README contains an extensive privacy and security section covering what leaves the vault and how CLI backends are contained.
intentEvidence: Not a chat sidebar you copy-paste into
motivation: The author built it on the philosophy of bringing the language model into the editing and thinking process instead of exiting into a chat interface, crediting Maggie Appleton's daemon concept and Juri Strumpflohner's AI-first markdown editor demos.
problem: Getting AI feedback in Obsidian usually means leaving the editor for a chat window and pasting text back and forth, with no anchored, reviewable edits inside the note.

requires.name: API key for a hosted backend (Anthropic, OpenAI, OpenRouter, Azure OpenAI)
Claude Code or Codex CLI for local agent backends

summary: AI editing plugin that runs configurable reviewer personas over notes and shows anchored findings with inline diffs you accept or reject.
